transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
Ukrainian President Zelensky tells the BBC he found it strange that President Trump calls Russian leader Vladimir Putin a friend.
NPR's Joanna Kekisis reports Zelensky also addressed the recent Ukrainian attack on a Russian warship.
Speaking to the BBC's Sarah Rainsford, Zelensky criticized Trump's friendly greeting of Putin at the recent trilateral summit in China.
Zelensky compared Putin to Adolf Hitler.
He's an aggressor and a killer. He can't be a friend.
It's the same that somebody say about Hitler during the Second World War, that he's a good friend. No.
Meanwhile, Zelensky also said Ukraine had coordinated with nearby countries when Ukrainian cedrones attacked a Russian warship off the coast of Libya.
Italy's foreign minister, though, told local media that Italy, which is near Libya, was not informed.
Joanna Kekisis, NPR News, Cave.
The World Health Organization says measles deaths around the world are at historic lows, but progress to eliminate the disease has been met with setbacks,
as many countries struggle to restore vaccination rates to pre-pandemic levels.
NPR's Maria Godoy has more.
The WHO says since 2000, vaccination efforts have helped reduce measles deaths worldwide by 91 percent to 72,000 deaths last year.
But many countries have also experienced backsliding.
The U.S., Bolivia, and Mexico all lost their measles elimination status last week.
Here's Dr. Kate O'Brien of the WHO.
I think this is the alarm bell for everybody around the world.
She says many people, including doctors, have not seen measles before.
But it is back, and the world is learning just how sick and just how dead measles can make you.
In the U.S., states have reported more than a dozen measles-related deaths so far this year.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
Today is Black Friday, the day when shoppers hope to get good deals.
Kelly O'Neill was at a mall in Glendale, California.
She says she looks forward to in-person shopping on Black Friday every year.
I do it every year.
Yeah. You know, I think the deals maybe haven't been as good recently as they used to be,
but it's still fun to get up and just be out when nobody else is and see what's out there.
Meghan Morgan was at a mall in Metairie, Louisiana.
It's lesser, but I mean, we're spending a little bit more, probably sparingly, than we used to.
But for the most part, we're just having a good time.
And if we see something that catches our eye and will make us happy,
then we're trying to get to the muse in the season.
Online shopping is growing, too, as people use AI tools to try to help them find the best deals.
Adobe Digital Insight says online spending yesterday was up 10 percent from last year,
as consumers spent a record $7.1 billion.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
U.S. military says it disabled another ship in the Gulf of Oman
that tried to breach a naval blockade on Iranian ports.
U.S. Central Command says the MV Pacific Archer was disabled yesterday
and that the civilian crew was unharmed.
The Pacific Archer is at least the 15th disclosed vessel
to be disabled by the U.S. military since the blockade started in the spring.
The Department of Education says it would spend $50 million in the coming years
to train aspiring and current teachers
to work with the country's growing population of people learning English.
And Pierce Janaki Mehta has more.
This investment in English learners comes as a bit of a surprise.
Considering that last year, the Trump administration ended 28 grants
aimed at English learners.
And when the department cut about half its staff,
almost everyone who worked on federal grants aimed at English learners was laid off.
At the time, the administration said the grants didn't align with its priorities.
Now it's funding 12 new grant projects that will help colleges partner with school districts
to provide training and support to new and existing teachers who work with English learners.
This is a big area of need as the number of students who are English learners
in this country continues to rise.
Janaki Mehta, NPR News.
Wall Street soared today on this holiday-shortened trading week.
By the closing bell, the Dow was up 591 points, that's up 1.1 percent.
The Nasdaq up 543 points, that's up 2.3 percent.
The S&P 500 gained 114 points, that's up 1.6 percent.
You're listening to NPR News.

topics.text: Zelensky tells BBC that Trump calling Putin a friend is strange, compares Putin to Hitler
Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship off Libya; Italy says it was not informed
WHO says global measles deaths at historic lows, but elimination progress faces setbacks
Black Friday shoppers at malls in Glendale, California and Metairie, Louisiana
Online spending on Black Friday rises 10 percent to a record $7.1 billion, per Adobe
U.S. military disables another vessel, the MV Pacific Archer, trying to breach Iran port blockade
Education Department to spend $50 million training teachers of English learners
Wall Street surges on holiday-shortened week; Dow up 591 points, Nasdaq up 2.3 percent
